q-132173.name: Question 1
q-132173.problem: Given that the random variable $X∼\text{Exp}(\frac{1}{5}),$ calculate $P(X\le 2).$ Round your final answer to four decimal places.
q-132173.worked_solution:
An exponential random variable $X$ with rate $\lambda $ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\lambda {e}^{-\lambda x}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that

$$
X∼\text{Exp}(\frac{1}{5}).
$$

So, $X$ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{5}{e}^{-x/5}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate $P(X\le 2)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 2) & ={\int }_{0}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{1}{5}{e}^{-x/5}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{{e}^{-x/5}|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =-{e}^{-2/5}+{e}^{0} \\  & ≈0.3297\end{aligned}
$$

f(x)={λe−λx,x≥00,otherwise

q-132179.name: Question 2
q-132179.problem: Given that the random variable $X∼\text{Exp}(\sqrt{3}),$ calculate $P(X<\frac{1}{3}).$ Round your final answer to four decimal places.
q-132179.worked_solution:
An exponential random variable $X$ with rate $\lambda $ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\lambda {e}^{-\lambda x}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that

$$
X∼\text{Exp}(\sqrt{3}).
$$

So, $X$ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\sqrt{3}{e}^{-\sqrt{3}x}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate $P(X<\frac{1}{3})$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<\frac{1}{3}) & ={\int }_{0}^{1/3}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1/3}\sqrt{3}{e}^{-\sqrt{3}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{e}^{-\sqrt{3}x}{|}_{0}^{1/3} \\  & =-{e}^{-\sqrt{3}/3}+{e}^{0} \\  & ≈0.4386\end{aligned}
$$

q-132193.name: Question 3
q-132193.problem: Given that the random variable $X∼\text{Exp}(\sqrt{2}),$ calculate $P(X>\sqrt{2}).$ Round your final answer to four decimal places.
q-132193.worked_solution:
An exponential random variable $X$ with rate $\lambda $ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\lambda {e}^{-\lambda x}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that

$$
X∼\text{Exp}(\sqrt{2}).
$$

So, $X$ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2}{e}^{-\sqrt{2}x}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate $P(X>\sqrt{2})$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>\sqrt{2}) & ={\int }_{\sqrt{2}}^{\infty }f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\sqrt{2}}^{\infty }\sqrt{2}{e}^{-\sqrt{2}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{e}^{-\sqrt{2}x}{|}_{\sqrt{2}}^{\infty } \\  & ={e}^{-2} \\  & ≈0.1353\end{aligned}
$$

q-96347.name: Question 5
q-96347.problem: Given that the random variable $X∼\text{Exp}(\frac{1}{3}),$ calculate $P(2<X<3).$ Round your final answer to four decimal places.
q-96347.worked_solution:
An exponential random variable $X$ with rate $\lambda $ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\lambda {e}^{-\lambda x}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that

$$
X∼\text{Exp}(\frac{1}{3}).
$$

So, $X$ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}{e}^{-x/3}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate $P(2<X<3)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(2<X<3) & ={\int }_{2}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{3}\frac{1}{3}{e}^{-x/3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{e}^{-x/3}{|}_{2}^{3} \\  & =-{e}^{-1}+{e}^{-2/3} \\  & ≈0.1455\end{aligned}
$$

q-96421.name: Question 6
q-96421.problem: Given that the random variable $X∼\text{Exp}(1),$ calculate $P(0.5\le X\le 2).$ Round your final answer to four decimal places.
q-96421.worked_solution:
An exponential random variable $X$ with rate $\lambda $ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\lambda {e}^{-\lambda x}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that

$$
X∼\text{Exp}(1).
$$

So, $X$ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}{e}^{-x}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate $P(0.5\le X\le 2)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.5\le X\le 2) & ={\int }_{0.5}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0.5}^{2}{e}^{-x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{e}^{-x}{|}_{0.5}^{2} \\  & =-{e}^{-2}+{e}^{-0.5} \\  & ≈0.4712\end{aligned}
$$

q-253935.name: Question 7
q-253935.problem: Given that the random variable $X∼\text{Exp}(3),$ calculate $P(X\le \frac{5}{6}\,|\,X>\frac{2}{3}).$
q-253935.worked_solution:
Given a random variable $X∼Exp(\lambda ),$ and two positive real numbers $s,t,$ the memoryless property of the exponential distribution states that

$$
P(X>s+t\,|\,X>s)=P(X>t)={e}^{-\lambda t}.
$$

We can compute the complementary conditional probability as follows:

$$
P(X\le s+t\,|\,X>s)=1-P(X>s+t\,|\,X>s)=1-{e}^{-\lambda t}
$$

In our case, we have $\lambda =3,$ $s=\frac{2}{3},$ and $s+t=\frac{5}{6}.$ From this, we can find $t$ as follows:

$$
t=(t+s)-s=\frac{5}{6}-\frac{2}{3}=\frac{1}{6}
$$

Substituting these values into the above formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le \frac{5}{6}\,|\,X>\frac{2}{3}) & =1-{e}^{-\lambda t} \\  & =1-{e}^{-(3)\cdot (1/6)} \\  & =1-{e}^{-1/2}\end{aligned}
$$

q-253936.name: Question 8
q-253936.problem: Given that the random variable $X∼\text{Exp}(\frac{3}{5}),$ calculate $P(X\le 9\,|\,X>4).$
q-253936.worked_solution:
Given a random variable $X∼Exp(\lambda ),$ and two positive real numbers $s,t,$ the memoryless property of the exponential distribution states that

$$
P(X>s+t\,|\,X>s)=P(X>t)={e}^{-\lambda t}.
$$

We can compute the complementary conditional probability as follows:

$$
P(X\le s+t\,|\,X>s)=1-P(X>s+t\,|\,X>s)=1-{e}^{-\lambda t}
$$

In our case, we have $\lambda =\frac{3}{5},$ $s=4,$ and $s+t=9.$ From this, we can find $t$ as follows:

$$
t=(t+s)-s=9-4=5
$$

Substituting these values into the above formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 9\,|\,X>4) & =1-{e}^{-\lambda t} \\  & =1-{e}^{-(3/5)\cdot (5)} \\  & =1-{e}^{-3}\end{aligned}
$$

q-253936.html:
Question 8
?

Given that the random variable X∼Exp(35), calculate P(X≤9|X>4).

a
 3e−1/5
b
 1−5e−3/5
c
 e−3
d
 1−e−1/5
e
 1−e−3
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Given a random variable X∼Exp(λ), and two positive real numbers s,t, the memoryless property of the exponential distribution states that P(X>s+t|X>s)=P(X>t)=e−λt.

We can compute the complementary conditional probability as follows: P(X≤s+t|X>s)=1−P(X>s+t|X>s)=1−e−λt

In our case, we have λ=35, s=4, and s+t=9. From this, we can find t as follows: t=(t+s)−s=9−4=5

Substituting these values into the above formula, we get P(X≤9|X>4)=1−e−λt=1−e−(3/5)⋅(5)=1−e−3
